verdicts.quote: one of the flat surfaces or straight edges of something
verdicts.reason: A side can be a curved surface, as with a can or a ball, so the definition is too narrow.

verdicts.quote: In British English, **side** also means a sports team (*the home side*).
verdicts.reason: This is not limited to British English; American English also uses side to mean a team, especially in formal sports contexts.
The food sense is standard rather than informal, and side meaning a side dish is also used outside American English.

verdicts.quote: in addition to your main job, often secretly; or served in a separate dish
verdicts.reason: Work done on the side is usually additional to a main job but is not inherently secret.

verdicts.quote: to be careful and avoid risk, even if it is probably not needed
verdicts.reason: The definition begins with an infinitive; verb and phrase definitions must use a base-form verb phrase without "to".

reviewers.summary: Most fields are sound. The main corrections concern the overly narrow surface definition, inaccurate regional and register claims, the misleading secrecy implication in "on the side," and one missing common sense.
The entry is well-structured and follows the house rules.
